intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene (602243) on chromosome 11p15.5.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3 patients are homozygous for a single nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151, causing a frameshift and premature stop signal at codon 140.
checks.explanation: Patients with nephritis, deafness and pretibial EB are homozygous for a CD151 truncating mutation; the authors conclude CD151 is essential in kidney and skin. The EBS7 name is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: The CD151 gene is located on chromosome 11p15.5.
checks.evidence_quote: It is encoded by a gene at the same position on chromosome 11p15.5 as the MER2 blood group gene.

paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is an autosomal recessive disorder. Its features are hereditary nephritis that progresses to end-stage renal disease, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa and sensorineural deafness. Patients lack the MER2 blood group antigen, which is carried by CD151 on erythrocytes (Karamatic Crew et al., 2004).

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3 patients are homozygous for a single nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151
checks.explanation: The abstract never names an inheritance mode. Autosomal recessive inheritance is only implied by the patients being homozygous, 2 of them sibs.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) studied 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, 2 of whom were sibs. All 3 were homozygous for a 1-bp insertion (G383) in exon 5 of the CD151 gene. The insertion caused a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140. The authors predicted that the truncated protein would lack its integrin-binding domain.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) reported that CD151 forms stable laminin-binding complexes with integrins. They concluded that CD151 is essential for the correct assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membranes in the kidney and that it has functional significance in the skin. They suggested that CD151 is probably a component of the inner ear and that it could play a role in erythropoiesis.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) studied 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, 2 of whom were sibs. The sibs also had sensorineural deafness, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa and beta-thalassemia minor. All 3 patients were homozygous for a 1-bp insertion (G383) in exon 5 of the CD151 gene. The insertion caused a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140. The authors predicted that the truncated protein would lack its integrin-binding domain.
